value.rationale: A priced network class can uniquely favor buying a costly whole edge orbit for an intermediate observation horizon while correctly omitting it at both shorter and longer horizons. The two-switch phenomenon is restricted to exactly the one-vertex imbalance \(q=p+1\), with explicit sharp price ceiling and nonvanishing \(O(1/p)\) critical window. It is a substantive finite-time intervention design boundary, directly contrasting the published asymptotic spectral-gap allocation on the identical networks; it is not an arbitrary parameter slice or numerical-table recomputation.
